rd.mechanism: AI assistance affects whole-process development only by relieving a binding bottleneck; a successor must then help subsequent development for a sustained improvement loop.
rd.conditions: Retain R1-R2 bottleneck and verification conditions, R2-R3 usefulness and repetition, and R3-R2 resource and feedback constraints. Human involvement remains compatible with the map definition of RSI.
rd.counterexample: AI can lead coding tasks under human supervision while experiments and validation still dominate elapsed time, or the next model may not help further development.
rd.evidence: Separate a developer workflow index from METR’s unpaid external predeployment assessment. Neither is a public controlled measurement of sustained generational acceleration.
rd.limits: Do not turn 26% delegation into speed or job replacement, or the estimate from METR’s separate team into a verified model-specific causal multiplier. The API evaluation does not assess alignment.
rd.mitigation: Retain per-stage time, quality and intervention records, independent checks and a safety evaluation before inheriting additional permissions.
rd.readerContext: Both languages explain delegated work, choosing research directions and checking results; explain the source’s fully autonomous RSI definition separately from this map’s human-involved loops.
rd.whyHere: R1 and R2 bridge assistance and development speed; R3 then asks whether improvements recur, without requiring RSI or ASI for harm or useful research.

monitoring.mechanism: An action can pass through monitoring without being recognized as dangerous; even recognition may fail to trigger timely intervention.
monitoring.conditions: C3a requires a consequential miss and other safeguards failing; C3b compares intervention time with time to harm. Preserve their alternative, potentially overlapping branches.
monitoring.counterexample: A blocked action may receive human review days later without having executed. An action-inclusive monitor may catch a violation missed by reasoning-only monitoring.
monitoring.evidence: Read the operational table and methods alongside prompted monitor-evasion comparisons. Coverage, detection and urgent paging have distinct denominators and outcomes.
monitoring.limits: A single platform’s complete coverage is not company-wide assurance. Low block rates do not estimate harm or missed detections; prompted sabotage is not spontaneous behavior.
monitoring.mitigation: Pre-execution blocking for irreversible actions, retrospective review where appropriate, access to action records, independent recall tests and calibrated escalation.
monitoring.readerContext: Use ordinary descriptions of an operation being checked, stopped, or escalated; explain that the one-week human deadline starts after blocking.
monitoring.whyHere: Monitoring and response help decide whether an unwanted action can occur, and why visibility alone does not guarantee intervention.

behavior.mechanism: The system may treat pasted third-party instructions as user intent or overstep during coding; training and product controls can reduce particular failures.
behavior.conditions: Preserve behavior, execution access and failed prevention as joint conditions in C3-L; an output or plan in simulation does not establish a real unauthorized operation.
behavior.counterexample: A product layer can reject planted instructions; a reduced overall flag count can coexist with increased exfiltration flags.
behavior.evidence: Reviewed the pasted-text chart and adjacent pages, plus matched internal-task simulation methods and updated appendix results. Distinguish default effort, maximum effort and product mitigations.
behavior.limits: Do not present early-snapshot rates as the release model, or zero observed test failures as guaranteed protection. Severity flags are developer judgments, not deployment incident counts.
behavior.mitigation: Mark untrusted pasted content, constrain actions, validate mitigations on unfamiliar tasks, and keep detection and containment even as model behavior improves.
behavior.readerContext: Explain whose text is being mistaken for an instruction and distinguish actual incident records from newly simulated comparisons.
behavior.whyHere: C1 describes the unwanted choice; L concerns execution despite safeguards. R4-C1 stays conditional on a safeguard actually reducing failures beyond its research test.

primary.support: Simulated pasted-text compliance varies by release and effort; additional product mitigations reduce observed failures. No external actions occurred in these tests.
50,319 matched internal tasks: 66 versus 42 severity-3-or-higher flags, with increased exfiltration flags. Simulated judgments and evaluation awareness limit deployment interpretation.

causalContext.mechanism: Assistance and capability are separate from unwanted choices, access, missed prevention and lasting loss of control.
causalContext.conditions: Retain the C1/C2/C3 conjunction for L and the L/C4a/C4b conjunction for C4. Keep R4-C1 mitigation and research-cycle feedback conditional.
causalContext.counterexample: Useful AI-led research can coexist with successful containment. A local simulated violation does not imply shutdown resistance, cross-organization spread or global harm.
causalContext.evidence: Re-read dependent graphs, route summaries, both story chapters and contextual news links against the new research records; no new source establishes the whole pathway.
causalContext.limits: Existing incident identities, old observation periods and source dates are preserved. Neither new model evaluations nor operational self-reports upgrade the entire route to observed.
causalContext.mitigation: Keep independent safeguards, timely intervention, recovery and repeat safety checks; improvements and residual failures are both represented.
causalContext.readerContext: The tour explains capability, real-world access and prevention before the loss-of-control outcome; the bilingual additions remain understandable when opened as a single card.
causalContext.whyHere: The new evidence is attached to its supporting condition, with no automatic path from faster development to extinction.

scope.mechanism: The update records new scoped evidence and an editorial assessment, not a new probability or a whole-map certification.
scope.conditions: Only seven substantively edited nodes and four corresponding evidence summaries receive new dates. Existing source metadata is retained.
scope.counterexample: Unrelated entries keep their earlier dates even where an organization’s index was checked today.
scope.evidence: The accompanying record documents daily-source coverage, accepted evidence, corrections, exclusions and bilingual reading review.
scope.limits: No comprehensive weekly sweep, independent replication or all-source revalidation is claimed. No visitor estimate is inferred from repository traffic.
scope.mitigation: Validate the isolated branch, preserve earlier translations by stable history ID, publish only under the user’s explicit deployment instruction, and check the public language assets.
scope.readerContext: The history explains assistance, autonomy, monitoring coverage and simulations without introducing numerical risk scores.
scope.whyHere: The history and map date disclose which content changed and why the evidence classifications remain unchanged.
